name: Browser & Web Application Security
description: Browser & Web Application Security standard. Defines enforceable rules, implementation boundaries, failure handling and review evidence expected when STD-WEB-SEC applies.

rules.title: Prevent script injection by default
rules.detail: Rely on framework escaping, avoid unsafe HTML sinks, sanitize explicitly allowed rich content and apply a restrictive Content Security Policy where feasible.
rules.example_good: The implementation and review evidence demonstrate: Prevent script injection by default.
rules.example_bad: The change violates or ignores the rule: Prevent script injection by default.

rules.title: Protect browser sessions and cookies
rules.detail: Session cookies containing credentials use Secure, HttpOnly and appropriate SameSite settings; session rotation and expiry follow authentication risk.
rules.example_good: The implementation and review evidence demonstrate: Protect browser sessions and cookies.
rules.example_bad: The change violates or ignores the rule: Protect browser sessions and cookies.

rules.title: Protect state-changing requests against CSRF where cookie authentication is used
rules.detail: Use same-site policy plus CSRF token/origin validation appropriate to the architecture.
rules.example_good: The implementation and review evidence demonstrate: Protect state-changing requests against CSRF where cookie authentication is used.
rules.example_bad: The change violates or ignores the rule: Protect state-changing requests against CSRF where cookie authentication is used.

rules.title: Restrict cross-origin access explicitly
rules.detail: CORS uses an allowlist of required origins/methods/headers; credentials are never combined with wildcard origins.
rules.example_good: The implementation and review evidence demonstrate: Restrict cross-origin access explicitly.
rules.example_bad: The change violates or ignores the rule: Restrict cross-origin access explicitly.

rules.title: Prevent clickjacking and unsafe navigation
rules.detail: Use frame-ancestors/X-Frame-Options as appropriate and validate redirect/return URLs against trusted destinations.
rules.example_good: The implementation and review evidence demonstrate: Prevent clickjacking and unsafe navigation.
rules.example_bad: The change violates or ignores the rule: Prevent clickjacking and unsafe navigation.

rules.title: Do not store long-lived secrets in browser-readable storage
rules.detail: Tokens or sensitive secrets accessible to JavaScript require explicit threat review; prefer secure server-managed sessions where appropriate.
rules.example_good: The implementation and review evidence demonstrate: Do not store long-lived secrets in browser-readable storage.
rules.example_bad: The change violates or ignores the rule: Do not store long-lived secrets in browser-readable storage.

integration_guide.title: Resolve applicability and dependencies
integration_guide.description: Confirm where STD-WEB-SEC applies and resolve its extends/implements/uses/aligns_with dependencies in the project standard profile.

integration_guide.title: Record project decisions
integration_guide.description: Apply the rules of Browser & Web Application Security to requirements/design/ADRs and record any project-specific thresholds, providers or justified exceptions.

integration_guide.title: Implement with evidence
integration_guide.description: Implement the applicable MUST/SHOULD rules and link code, configuration, tests or review evidence to the change.

integration_guide.title: Verify before completion
integration_guide.description: Run automated checks where possible and manual review for judgement-based rules; close or approve documented deviations.

common_issues.issue: Browser & Web Application Security is applied inconsistently across features
common_issues.cause: The project references the standard but does not resolve concrete ownership, thresholds or verification evidence.
common_issues.solution: Resolve dependencies, record project-specific decisions and include applicable rules in implementation/review checks.

common_issues.issue: Implementation satisfies the happy path but misses Browser & Web Application Security failure cases
common_issues.cause: Boundary, retry, security or recovery scenarios were not included in acceptance/test planning.
common_issues.solution: Use the standard rules to add explicit failure/recovery scenarios and verify them before release.
